# Qiyas bench

2026-11-13 04:57. The bench's process opted out of Windows' power throttling (every subject at the speed the hardware gives). Median wall time (ms); `×` = adad ÷ subject (above 1: faster than adad). `err` = largest |result − float64 math on the same stored inputs| as the type defines the result (a type that is not float: rounded as it rounds and held to its range; a float type: held where it saturates). `lane` = what the subject computed in.

The readout: `bytes` and `ops` are what the row's operation moves and computes by its own definition (every operand read once and every result written once at its stored width; each arithmetic operation or elementary function one, a multiply-add two); `bound` is the time those take at this device's limits, measured at the start of this run (the larger of the bytes at the memory's measured rates, reads at the read rate and writes at the write rate or a copy's mix at the copy rate, whichever model is fastest, and the operations at the lane's peak; `by` names which: memory, copy where the row does not say which bytes it writes, or the lane); each subject's `rate` is what it reached in the bound's unit and `of bound` the bound ÷ its time; `held` a bound on the working memory its run held beyond its operands (host: the pooled buffers out at once at their peak, every other allocation as if all were live together, and the subject's kept buffers, each thread's peak summed; + device on a GPU, the subject's buffers at their peak; ? where the subject cannot tell).

Proof: the CUDA rows: the checks not run, build 059aa0daff05ecf7 had passed them on every device benched. The CPU rows: the checks not run: build cd8011c51a4114c6 had passed them on every device benched.

Builds: the CUDA rows are the full readout of build b36cb4a (2026-11-13 04:57, the CUDA part of a cuda,cpu run), with 11 rows re-timed on that build, the box-loss rows on 8db7cc0 and 22689b7 and the float64 erf rows on 03a6098 (notes at the end); the CPU rows are the CPU-only readout of build ac1f23a (2026-11-13 16:35, a process of its own), the rows more than 10 % off their previous reading re-timed on that build (notes at the end).
